[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Charles Glesgowe was baptised on 10 October 1686 at South Leith, Midlothian, Scotland, a child of [[Glasgow-3012|John Glasgow]] and [[Currie-4998|Margaret Currie]].<ref name="FSBaptism">“Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4J-JJK : accessed 16 September 2021), John Glesgowe in the entry for Charles Glesgowe, 1686.</ref><ref>“Scotland, Select Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, Ancestry ([https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/60143/records/21451068 record 21451068] : accessed 30 August 2026), Charles Glesgowe, 1686; extracted index, original register image not inspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-3012]] is assessed at 82% (probable). Charles’s 1686 South Leith baptism names John Glesgowe and Margaret Currie. The existing John account includes the 1673 Kirknewton marriage to Margaret Currie and the 1676 Glencorse child household, giving a particular couple and compatible sequence across nearby Lothian parishes.

Complete selected father-profile placement82%; John’s 1649 childhood identification and Charles’s claimed Irish adulthood remain unproved. Charles James is not the register’s compound forename.

Next useful test: Test the 1673 groom’s identity and the Scottish-to-Irish Charles continuation separately.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4J-JJK “Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4J-JJK : accessed 16 September 2021), John Glesgowe in the entry for Charles Glesgowe, 1686.]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.



=== Scottish child versus Cross identity ===

The extracted baptism indexes establish the Scottish child and named parents. No reviewed record shows that this child migrated to Cross, County Londonderry, or that he became the father of [[Glasgow-2916|James Glasgow]]. Chronological fit and an uncommon given name are not an identity bridge.

The structured Cross death place and the son link are retained as uncertain research claims pending an evidenced replacement. The [[Space:Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland|Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland]] study and a user-submitted MyHeritage tree preserve the proposed Derry lineage as leads, not as independent proof.<ref name="IrelandStudy">[[Space:Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland|Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland]], accessed 19 August 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.myheritage.com/profile-798694011-2003650/charles-james-glasgow MyHeritage user-submitted tree for Charles James Glasgow]; unsourced and used only as a lead.</ref>

The 1740 Ulster religious return shows contemporary Glasgow households at Tamlaght O'Crilly and Derryloran but does not identify Charles or bridge him to the Scottish baptism.<ref>[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740religiousreturnsulstername.pdf 1740 Protestant Householders' Return for Ulster], surname index.</ref> PRONI's guide lists Derryloran baptisms only from 1795/1797 and Cookstown Presbyterian baptisms from 1822 or later.<ref>[https://www.proni.gov.uk/publications/proni-guide-church-records Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Guide to Church Records''], Derryloran and Cookstown entries; consulted 30 August 2026.</ref> That survival gap explains why ordinary parish-register searches cannot bridge the Scottish child to Ireland. Deeds, estate papers, probate, religious returns and migration evidence are the appropriate next sources.
